name.text: Types of Functions — matching a key feature to a function type

questiontext.text:
Which type of function is best described by the following feature?

"{@featuretext@}"

[[input:ans1]] [[validation:ans1]]

generalfeedback.text:
This feature is the defining characteristic of a {@ta@} function.

  • A linear function \(y = mx + c\) changes by the same amount for every unit step in \(x\) (a constant rate of change \(m\)), so its graph is a straight line.
  • A quadratic function \(y = ax^2 + bx + c\) has a parabola as its graph, with exactly one turning point (the vertex) and a vertical line of symmetry through it.
  • A cubic function \(y = ax^3 + bx^2 + cx + d\) has exactly one point of inflection and either two turning points or none; one end of the graph goes up and the other goes down.
  • An exponential function such as \(y = 2^x\) or \(y = \left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)^x\) approaches a horizontal asymptote on one side and grows more and more steeply on the other.

questiondescription.text: Grade 11 Functions 16.5 (Types of Functions). Reasons about the defining graphical feature of linear, quadratic, cubic, and exponential functions, rather than reading a specific graph or formula.

falsefeedback.text: Picture the graph of each family: a straight line, a U-shaped parabola, an S-shaped cubic, and an exponential curve that levels off towards an asymptote. Which one has exactly the feature described?
